progressAssistant.title: LexiFox
progressAssistant.greeting: Hi! Choose a question and I’ll explain only what the recorded LexiPlay activity supports.
progressAssistant.note: LexiFox explains recorded LexiPlay activity only. It does not diagnose learning differences or replace professional assessment.

questions.summary: How is my child doing overall?
questions.routine: How can we build a good routine?
questions.session: What should we do in the next session?

answers.summaryEmptyBody: There is no recorded activity yet. Start with one short game together and focus on making the experience positive.
answers.summaryEmptyTip1: Choose a game that looks fun or familiar.
answers.summaryEmptyTip2: Keep the first session to around 5 minutes.
answers.summaryBody: {{name}} has {{minutes}} minutes of recorded activity across {{days}} active day(s) and {{games}} game(s).
answers.streakTip: Current practice streak: {{days}} day(s). Short, repeatable sessions are valuable.
answers.noStreakTip: A short predictable practice moment can help build a routine.
answers.averageTip: The current average is {{minutes}} minutes per active day.
answers.activityRecordedTip: Activity is recorded. More playtime will make the overview more detailed.
answers.strengthBody: {{game}} has the strongest recorded score: {{score}}% across {{sessions}} completed session(s).
answers.strengthTip1: Use this game as a confidence-building start to a session.
answers.strengthTip2: Praise effort and strategies, not only the score.
answers.progressBody: {{game}} currently shows the furthest recorded progress at level {{level}}, word {{word}}. There are no accuracy scores yet, so LexiFox cannot compare strengths fairly.
answers.progressTip1: Celebrate returning to the game and moving forward one step at a time.
answers.progressTip2: Keep using familiar activities to build confidence.
answers.activityBody: {{name}} has recorded activity. As more rounds are completed, LexiFox can describe game-specific patterns more clearly.
answers.activityTip: Praise trying, listening, and returning to practice.
answers.focusBody: {{game}} has a recorded score of {{score}}% across {{sessions}} completed session(s). Try a few relaxed attempts before increasing difficulty.
answers.focusTip1: Repeat one familiar level before making it harder.
answers.focusTip2: Stop while the child still feels successful and engaged.
answers.focusProgressBody: {{game}} has the furthest recorded progress, so it is a sensible familiar activity for the next practice. No score data is available yet, so this is not a judgement about ability.
answers.focusProgressTip1: Begin with one familiar round before trying something new.
answers.focusProgressTip2: Let the child choose whether to continue or switch games.
answers.focusStartBody: Activity has been recorded, but no game progress is available yet. A familiar, enjoyable game is the best next step.
answers.focusStartTip: Keep the next session short and finish with encouragement.
answers.routineGreatBody: A {{days}}-day streak shows a strong routine. Keep protecting this calm, predictable learning moment.
answers.routineGrowingBody: {{days}} days in a row is a promising start. A short daily rhythm can make practice feel easier.
answers.routineBody: There is recorded activity, but not a consistent streak yet. Short, regular sessions are usually easier to sustain than occasional long sessions.
answers.routineTip1: Aim for 5–10 minutes at a calm, predictable time of day.
answers.routineTip2: Offer a choice between two games so the child has some control.
answers.routineTip3: Take a short movement or water break if practice becomes tiring.
answers.sessionBody: For the next session, begin with {{game}}. Keep it short, let {{name}} set the pace, and finish with a specific compliment.
answers.sessionNoGameBody: For the next session, let the child choose one available game. Keep it short, calm, and encouraging.
answers.sessionTip1: Start by saying: “Let’s try one small challenge together.”
answers.sessionTip2: Finish with a clear compliment about effort, listening, or persistence.
answers.sessionHeartsTip: Some games are resting, so choose another available game or take a break.
